en: Majjhima Nikāya 145,
Puṇṇovādasutta:
Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Then, in the evening, the Venerable Puṇṇa emerged from seclusion and approached the Blessed One;
having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable...
Puṇṇa said this to the Blessed One:

“It would be well, Bhante, if the Blessed One would exhort me with a brief exhortation, so that having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute.
“In that case, Puṇṇa, listen and pay close attention; I shall speak.”
“Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Puṇṇa replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Puṇṇa, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, pleasing, dear, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust.
If a bhikkhu delights in that, welcomes it, and remains clinging to it,
delight arises in him as he delights in it, welcomes it, and remains clinging to it.
"With the arising of delight comes the arising of suffering," Puṇṇa, I say.
"There are, Puṇṇa, sounds cognizable by the ear...
odors cognizable by the nose...
flavors cognizable by the tongue..."
Tangible objects cognizable by the body...
mental phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust—
if a bhikkhu delights in them, welcomes them, and remains attached to them.
For one who delights in that, welcomes it, and remains attached to it, delight arises.
"From the arising of delight comes the arising of suffering," Puṇṇa, I say.
And there are, Puṇṇa, forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, lovely, pleasing, endearing, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust.
If a bhikkhu does not delight in that, does not welcome it, and does not remain clinging to it,
then for him who does not delight in it, does not welcome it, and does not remain clinging to it, delight ceases.
“With the cessation of delight comes the cessation of suffering,” Puṇṇa, I say.
And yet, Puṇṇa, there are sounds cognizable by the ear...
odors cognizable by the nose...
flavors cognizable by the tongue...
Tangible objects cognizable by the body...
mental phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual pleasure, and provocative of lust—
if a bhikkhu does not delight in them, does not welcome them, and does not remain clinging to them;
"For one who does not delight in that, who does not welcome it, and who remains without clinging to it, delight ceases.
'With the cessation of delight comes the cessation of suffering,' Puṇṇa, I say.
And now, Puṇṇa, having been exhorted by me with this brief instruction, in which country will you dwell?"
“Venerable sir, having been exhorted by this brief exhortation from the Blessed One, there is a country named Sunāparanta; there I shall dwell.
“But, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta are fierce;
the people of Sunāparanta are harsh.”
“If, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta abuse and revile you, what will you think about that?
“If, Bhante, the people of Sunāparanta abuse and revile me, I will think:
‘These people of Sunāparanta are indeed good; these people of Sunāparanta are truly excellent, in that they do not strike me with their hands.’”
“It will be so here, Blessed One; it will be so here, Sugata.
“But if, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with their hand, what will you think of that, Puṇṇa?”
“Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta give me a blow with their hand, it will occur to me:
‘These people of Sunāparanta are indeed excellent, these people of Sunāparanta are truly noble, in that they do not give me a blow with a clod.
Thus it will be there, Blessed One.”
“In this matter, Sugata, it shall be so.
“But if, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta should strike you with clods of earth, what will you do then, Puṇṇa?
“If, Bhante, the people of Sunāparanta should strike me with clods of earth, then this will be my thought:”
“‘How fortunate indeed are these people of Sunāparanta! How truly blessed are these people of Sunāparanta! For they do not strike me with a staff.
Thus it shall be here, Blessed One;
thus it shall be here, Sugata.”
“But if, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with a staff, what will you think then, Puṇṇa?
“If, Bhante, the people of Sunāparanta give me a blow with a staff, I will think:
‘These people of Sunāparanta are indeed excellent; these people of Sunāparanta are truly kind, in that they do not strike me with a weapon.’”
“It will be so here, Blessed One; it will be so here, Sugata.
“But if, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with a weapon, what will you think then, Puṇṇa?”
“Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta should give me a blow with a weapon, it would occur to me:
‘These people of Sunāparanta are indeed excellent, these people of Sunāparanta are truly kind, in that they do not deprive me of life with a sharp weapon.
It will be thus for me there, Blessed One.”
“In this way, Sugata, it will be for me here.
“But if, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta should deprive you of life with a sharp weapon, what will you think then, Puṇṇa?
“If, Bhante, the people of Sunāparanta should deprive me of life with a sharp weapon, then I will think thus:”

“There are indeed disciples of the Blessed One who, being repelled, ashamed, and disgusted by the body and by life, seek for an executioner. This executioner has been found by me even before I sought him.
“So it shall be here, Blessed One; so it shall be here, Sugata,” he said.
“Excellent, excellent, Puṇṇa!
Endowed with this self-subduing tranquility, you will indeed be able to dwell in the Sunāparanta country.
Now, Puṇṇa, do as you think it is time to do.”
Then the Venerable Puṇṇa, having rejoiced and delighted in the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One,
and keeping him to his right, put away his lodging, took his bowl and robe,
and set out on a wandering tour toward the Sunāparanta country.
Wandering on his journey by stages, he arrived at the country of Sunāparanta.
There, indeed, the Venerable Puṇṇa dwelt in the country of Sunāparanta.

Then, during that very rainy season, the Venerable Puṇṇa ordained about five hundred lay followers; during that very rainy season, he ordained about five hundred female lay followers; and during that very rainy season, he realized the threefold knowledge.
Then, at a later time, the Venerable Puṇṇa attained final Nibbāna.

Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. As they were sitting there, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:
"Venerable sir, that clansman named Puṇṇa, who was instructed by the Blessed One with a brief exhortation, has passed away."
“What is his destination, what is his future state?
“Bhikkhus, the clansman Puṇṇa was wise; he practiced in accordance with the Dhamma and did not trouble me on account of the Dhamma.
Bhikkhus, the clansman Puṇṇa has attained final Nibbāna.”
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
Delighted, those bhikkhus rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Puṇṇovādasutta, the third, is finished.
